OSCP.packaging: Go proxy source ZIP containing an OSCP Cheat Sheet, contribution documents, CVE exploit subdirectories, and named Windows/Linux resources. There is no package install hook or archive entry point that deploys the tools. Dangerous code is openly documented and consistent with the training collection.
OSCP.SharpView.exe: IL entry point prints usage without arguments; otherwise Program.Run switches on the operator-selected method name. AD directory/account discovery, ACL changes, impersonation and Kerberos-related operations are exposed through that dispatcher. Costura embeds a supporting assembly. No unsolicited deployment or hidden callback was established.
OSCP.PowerUp.ps1: Defines PowerSploit audit/exploitation functions and Win32 interop scaffolding. Get-SiteListPassword recursively finds SiteList.xml and decrypts returned password fields. IIS AppCmd credential queries, Web.config connection-string decryption, EventVwr command-association UAC bypass and generated account/service helpers are real capabilities, retained. Module loading defines functions and interop; it does not unconditionally invoke the exploit suite.
OSCP.Seatbelt.exe: Program.Main enters Runtime command/group dispatch. WindowsVaultCommand calls VaultGetItem for the selected vault, marshals the returned structure, reads pAuthenticatorElement and formats the authenticator value. This supports the retained credential-extraction trait. LolbasCommand static initialization merely adds appvlp.exe to its inventory name set, refuting a signed-host staging claim.
OSCP.mimikatz.exe: Native command table maps UTF-16 pth at VA 0x14010fe48 to handler 0x1400b7068. LSASS acquisition references at 0x1400a142a/0x1400a1b85 lead to OpenProcess and security-package/module inspection. Memory-copy wrapper 0x1400099b0 dispatches to ReadProcessMemory at 0x140009bbc and WriteProcessMemory on its write branch. Credential recovery and pass-the-hash capabilities are retained; a training copy does not prove an unauthorized deployment.
OSCP.PrivescCheck.ps1: Decoded all 23 Base64/Gzip modules and inspected the load loop. It decodes/decompresses each module, calls NewScriptBlock and dot-sources it. The reflected GetMethod/Invoke evidence is a separate GetServiceHandle service-security query in the Shuddering module. The former hostile composite joined these independent operations and did not prove a reflected ScriptBlock execution chain.
OSCP.other_attack_resources: ASP.NET Page_Load calls CallbackShell with a private lab address; the connected socket becomes child stdin/stdout/stderr. The LNK downloads Powercat and invokes -c peer -p port -e powershell. The PHP Shell class connects with fsockopen, starts proc_open, and uses rw/brw helper methods to relay peer and process pipes. Looney Tunables exp.c constructs malformed nested GLIBC_TUNABLES, prepares a forged library path, forks and execves /usr/bin/su with that environment. SharpEfsPotato Main enables privileges, triggers EfsRpc authentication, duplicates the captured token and starts the supplied program. These supported attack behaviors remain visible.
OSCP.missing_context: No host telemetry, command history, deployment authorization, or upstream binary authenticity proof is supplied. The openly organized source/training bundle tips this archive to BENIGN; do not infer that every deployment of its tools is authorized.

SSS-decoded.ps1.path: Top-level Start-BeaconCycle checks whether aspnet_compiler is absent. It decodes Base64, XORs with the repeating UTF-8 key, interprets the result as another Base64 string, loads the reconstructed assembly, and invokes FILE.WHORE.LAUNCHER with a Framework aspnet_compiler.exe path and an embedded decimal MZ byte array. It repeats after a five-second delay. This process-liveness guard is a restart mechanism, not evidence of sandbox detection; the PowerShell loop itself is not a network beacon.
SSS-decoded.ps1.managed_loader: LAUNCHER calls the staged launcher up to five times. Its IL passes 0x08000004 suspended/no-window flags to a process-creation delegate, parses replacement PE headers/sections, writes replacement image data and updates saved thread context/entry before resuming. Dead invalid-token branches and mangled identifiers obstruct straightforward decompilation; dnfile/dncil recovered the live branch/delegate call paths.
SSS-decoded.ps1.native_payload: Recovered a native x86 Remcos agent. Rizin xrefs/disassembly establish the low-level keyboard hook (SetWindowsHookExA hook 13 at 0x40c0e4) and message loop, elevated COM moniker construction and CoGetObject at 0x408493, and suspended image replacement/context modification in 0x41c6f4. SETTINGS is loaded through FindResource/LoadResource/LockResource.
SSS-decoded.ps1.configuration: SETTINGS resource is 597 bytes. The first byte gives a 73-byte RC4 key; decrypting the remainder yields a controller at paticipa.home-webserver.de:9018 and artifact/logging settings. The endpoint was not contacted. This configured RAT plus its masked injector tips the verdict; no legitimate application function or training packaging accompanies this standalone script.
SSS-decoded.ps1.missing_context: Runtime launch success, architecture compatibility, operator identity and controller availability are unknown; they are not necessary to establish the supported malicious behavior.

cache-backdoor.php.path: Registers restoration on WordPress init. Restoration Base64-decodes and cyclic-XORs a packed payload, writes it to runtime.cache when missing, and overwrites .htaccess with AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .cache. Decoded bytes are another unauthenticated POST[command] -> proc_open -> stdout-echo shell. The outer script also contains that command path. The callback supplies durability and the handler makes the data-looking extension executable.
cache-backdoor.php.runtime_constraints: The outer script expects a WordPress bootstrap for add_action; the dropped command shell has no WordPress dependency. Apache handler overrides and writable paths affect runtime success. No authentication, nonce or restricted command set is present. No credential theft, network exfiltration, or privilege escalation is invented.

corrections.action: Removed unsupported composite; Base64 decoding, reflected method invocation, ScriptBlock construction and encoded module observations remain. No exact positive consumers existed. Actual PrivescCheck supplies a benign match, not merely a synthetic near miss.

Removed unsupported C2 inference. One IP-host PS1 URL could satisfy two any/needs legs; no tasking, beacon or execution relationship was required. Preserve the host/suffix/URL/download observations in neutral homes and detect the actual Powercat connection-to-shell pattern separately.

Moved the unchanged matcher, size floor and PEAS exclusion to micro-behaviors/fs/path/basename::appvlp-executable-reference at notable. Updated proxy-host-cluster to preserve its existing membership. The matcher proves neither signing nor staging.
Moved unchanged shape conditions to metadata/file/encoding::powershell-one-line-base64-data at notable. A one-line Base64-shaped source body proves encoding shape, not concealment.

Removed redundant OR with unsupported installation/lateral movement claim. Both PSEXESVC reference atoms and Sysinternals identities remain. Ancestor selectors still see the same source observations; no explicit consumer depended on this OR.

Moved raw-IP and onion host references, PS1 URL suffix, HTTP URL reference and download-method call to supported neutral homes at notable. Updated all exact consumers. Unfired legacy User-Agent rules were not changed semantically.

new_coverage.claim: Bounded co-occurrence of an established command shell and PHP handler with WordPress init, masked reconstruction and conditional missing-file recreation. No interprocedural payload-value proof is claimed.
Parsed PowerShell shortcut target plus Powercat connect/execute-shell command form.
One-class shell-property selection/use and bound connected-peer/proc_open-pipe helper argument pairs. The helper body remains opaque to the matcher, so no hostile direct-copy claim is made.

coverage_review.focused_controls: 13 positive and near-miss cases passed; see cases.json and verify.py.
coverage_review.material_losses: No supported attack mechanism was lost in the reviewed corpus. Removed hostile claims were unsupported co-occurrence or URL-only C2 inferences. Suspicious references/shape aggregates were retained as their actual neutral observations. The separate malicious LNK remains covered by five hostile COM-downloader/hidden-execution/staging/document-lure rules.
coverage_review.sharpview_output_variation: Standalone atomscan output omits 35 unchanged findings between runs, including 17 notable aggregates. Facts are identical; all 35 still MATCH in cleave test-rules (35 matched, 0 not matched), several explicitly marked as low-value any/needs output filtering. The archive SharpView member is stable at 108 findings. This is scan-output filtering variation, not a YAML matcher coverage regression.

remaining_disagreements: OSCP archive remains flagged at level 25/probability 0.99 despite its BENIGN training-bundle verdict. SharpView and PowerUp remain flagged; accurate credential/exploit/tool identity findings are intentionally retained. Seatbelt now leaves the calibrated flag grid; its real Vault extraction remains hostile.

The new PHP helper-wiring pattern is suspicious: the rule does not prove arbitrary helper implementations transfer bytes. Manual reverse engineering confirms the supplied helper-based reverse shell; no stronger generic runtime claim is added.

No classifier miss was exposed for the two MALICIOUS standalone scripts. SSS retains five hostile traits and the WordPress shell has four hostile findings spanning command access, handler abuse and recovery.
